hook: The Third Baptist Church complex, home since 1952 of a congregation founded in 1852, and San Francisco Landmark No. 275.

parcel.note: The 2025 roll records no building area for this parcel, which is exempt from taxation as religious property; it does carry an improvement value. The complex is three connected structures — sanctuary, detached bell tower, and the youth and classroom building.

permits.description: An 18-inch round city landmark plaque installed on the McAllister Street facade.
Entry service water lines repaired from the bell tower basement to the water heater room, about 50 linear feet, with 15 feet of exterior trench between the bell tower and the main church.
Emergency shoring of a staircase, with the permanent repair filed separately.
New subfloor and flooring; dishwasher relocated.
Equipment, appliances and finish flooring removed.
Two accessible doors installed in the gymnasium, with patching and paint.
Application to legalize an existing basement room and bathroom.
Accessible ramp installed at the gymnasium entrance.
Rear stair repaired; dry-rotted treads replaced.
Alterations or repairs; DBI records no description.

permit_summary.note: Three street-space and sidewalk permits are omitted from the timeline.

historical_record.description: The Third Baptist Church Complex was designated an Article 10 individual landmark by Ordinance 226-17, for its association with the congregation's role in the advancement of African Americans in San Francisco, with the Reverend Frederick Douglas Haynes Sr., and as one of the first Midcentury Modern ecclesiastical buildings in the Western Addition.
The cross that stands atop the bell tower was added.
The youth and classroom building, which houses the gymnasium on its second floor, was designed by architect Alfred W. Johnson and built as an addition.
The congregation moved to the Western Addition and commissioned architect William F. Gunnison to design the sanctuary and the detached bell tower that fronts McAllister Street.
The Reverend Frederick Douglas Haynes Sr. served as pastor. He ran for the San Francisco Board of Supervisors in 1945.
The congregation built a church at Hyde and Clay Streets on Nob Hill, where it remained for 44 years.
The congregation moved from Dupont Street to a building at Bush and Powell Streets, which the 1906 earthquake and fire destroyed.
The congregation took the name Third Baptist Church, as the third Baptist communion founded in the city and to be an inclusive church without a racial designation.

The congregation was founded as the First Colored Baptist Church of San Francisco, the first African American Baptist congregation west of the Rocky Mountains. Its first building stood on Dupont Street, now 1640–1644 Grant Avenue.

unknowns: The Argonaut dates the congregation's employment of its first pastor, the Reverend Charles Satchell, to 1854; SF Planning's landmark designation report dates it to 1856.

The Argonaut has the congregation beginning its activities on Dupont Street in 1852; the designation report has it forming that year at a private residence on Kearny Street and moving into the Dupont Street building in 1854.
The 2025 roll records no building area for this parcel.
